newsitem.title: USA: KazMinCo progress in copper/gold project.
newsitem.headline: KazMinCo progress in copper/gold project.

text.p: Kazakhstan Minerals Corp said it has received a positive pre-feasibility study for its Varvarinskoye gold/copper project in northern Kazakhstan and will proceed to a final feasibility study.
The pre-feasibility study, undertaken by Steffen Robertson and Kirsten, concluded that overall initial resource estimate is 2.74 million ounces of gold equivalent.
Mining is by open pit to 180 meters below, with initial annual production projected at 120,000 ounces. Start up costs would be US$90 million with payback over 2.2 years.
Metallurgical recoveries from the sulphide ores are 82 percent for gold and 92 percent for copper.
Cash operating costs are US$167 per ounce for the first nine years and then $197 per ounce over the full 13.5 year mine life.
"Current drilling is expected to add to proven and probable reserves," KazMinCo said in a statement.
The company will proceed to a final feasibility study including environmental approvals and detailed engineering.
A decision on whether to go ahead with the project is due by the end of the year. Project finance discussions have begun.
